scenario: [LTIM.10.9]: the engine refuses a host assert of a `TimeZoneOffset` fact whose `offset_s` is above 64800, with DS_ERR_INVAL (-1), and asserts nothing. The upper half of the range check; LTIM.10.9_offset_out_of_range_refused pins the lower. A good row is asserted first at +64800, the upper bound, admitted. Then a row at +64801, one second past it: refused at input 1, no fault event on the stream (a host refusal), and the engine unchanged (`fact_count_after` 1). What it discriminates: a runtime with no upper bound admits the second row and holds two facts; one whose bound is exclusive refuses the first row at input 0. PATH PINNED: libds's host-assert argument checks (`engine_assert_canonical`, wm.c), and Mercury's `ds.engine.host_assert_core` through `ltim_10_9_tz_row_fault`.
